title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 17-20 of the 'troisième mouture' of Analysis situs, June 1986). Grothendieck is building an axiomatics of 'tame' or stratified geometric objects without using a point-set topology.

Primitive data:
- M, a set of 'modèles' or pieces.
- F (script F), a set of 'figures', roughly finite unions or strata configurations of pieces.
- L, a set of 'lieux': idealised point-like places, treated as special elements.
- ≤, an adherence or containment relation, and ≪, a relation of being contained in the interior (relatively compact inside).
- X ∥ Y, disjointness; the barred symbol, 'not disjoint'.
- Omb(X), the 'ombre' (shadow) of X: the things Z with Z ≪ X. omb(X)° is the set of lieux interior to X.

On p.18 he stated At ens D, the 'set-theoretic disjunction criterion': X ∥ Y iff Omb X ∩ Omb Y = ∅, i.e. no Z ≪ X, Z ≪ Y. This page derives consequences.
- Cor 1: the same criterion holds for figures F, G.
- Cor 2: for a lieu x and a figure F, x ∥ F iff x is not ≪ F, i.e. x ∉ omb(F). Lieux behave as atoms, so meeting F means lying in its shadow.
- Cor 3: two lieux are disjoint iff they are distinct. Lieux behave exactly like points of a set.

NB: At ens D trivially implies At supp, the 'axiom of supports of a refinement' from p.18. That axiom says: if G ≪ X and some Y is disjoint from G but meets X, then such a Y can be chosen with Y ≪ X. The implication holds because, given such a Y, any Z in Omb Y ∩ Omb X works. He remarks that At supp holds in the frameworks he has in mind for practical purposes, but At ens D does not. So disjointness in his intended frameworks is not detected by common sub-pieces, i.e. the theory is genuinely not 'set-theoretic'.

He then introduces axioms involving lieux (AtL 1-3, 'axioms of divisibility').
- AtL 1: for every X ∈ M, omb(X)° ≠ ∅, i.e. every piece contains a lieu in its interior.
- His comment: this innocent-looking axiom implies, and in effect means, that the 'spaces' or 'lieux' are 'infinitely divisible'. They are neither discrete nor finite, so assuming it amounts to tacitly introducing 'actual infinity'.

The next page gives AtL 2: disjointness of X, Y is detected by pairwise disjointness of their lieux. This is weaker than set-theoretic disjointness of shadows. AtL 3 concerns lieux in different strata.

Overall purpose: a region-based ('pointless') foundation for stratified tame topology. Points (lieux) are a secondary, idealised notion whose existence is an axiom carrying the burden of the infinite.
errors: Cor 3 (x ∥ y iff x ≠ y) needs lieux to be minimal or atomic for ≪, so that omb(x) reduces to essentially {x}, plus some separation. This is implicit, not stated on the page.

The claim that AtL 1 'implies' infinite divisibility is informal. Existence of an interior lieu in every piece does not by itself force non-discreteness without further axioms, e.g. that a lieu is never itself a piece, or that X has proper sub-pieces disjoint from a given lieu. It is better read as a philosophical gloss than a theorem.

ideas.what: Disjointness criterion via common sub-pieces (shadows), with corollaries making lieux behave like points of a set
ideas.modern_name: Separativity / 'enough points' condition; in mereotopology, the extensionality of overlap
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), Tarski (geometry of solids, 1929), Clarke (1981); in locale theory, spatiality (Isbell, Johnstone)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the tame topology programme.

ideas.what: Distinguishing the weaker axiom At supp, valid in practical frameworks, from the set-theoretic At ens D, which fails there
ideas.modern_name: Non-spatial (pointless) region theories versus point-set models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Point-free topology (Johnstone 1983); contact algebras (de Vries 1962; Dimov-Vakarelov)

ideas.what: Existence of interior lieux in every piece (AtL 1), read as an infinite-divisibility axiom that introduces actual infinity
ideas.modern_name: Points as ideal elements in region-based geometry (Whitehead's abstractive classes; points of a locale via completely prime filters)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna; Stone duality tradition
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme criticises set-theoretic topology for tame purposes, but this axiom is not published.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's region-first axiomatics of tame topology (pieces, interior relation ≪, disjointness ∥, shadows, with lieux as axiomatised ideal points) is structurally a mereotopology / contact algebra. His observation that the set-theoretic disjunction criterion fails in his intended frameworks parallels the distinction between non-spatial and spatial region algebras. Neither the tame-topology literature (o-minimality) nor the mereotopology literature appears to have connected his Analysis situs notes with Whitehead–Tarski–de Vries region theories.
missed.quote: On notera que At supp est vérifié dans les cadres auxquels j'ai songé pour [fins] pratiques, mais non At ens D.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give a point-free axiomatisation of o-minimal or stratified tame geometry, linking region connection calculi and contact algebras to Grothendieck's tame topology programme.

missed.claim: The status of lieux (AtL 1-3) as optional axioms carrying 'actual infinity' suggests he intended a finitistic, pointless version of tame topology in which points are dispensable. As far as I know this was never developed.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on finitary or constructive foundations of tame geometry and on the definability of points in o-minimal structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual corollaries are routine consequences of the axioms. However, the explicit distinction between the region-based axiom At supp and the point-set axiom At ens D, and the reading of point-existence as the introduction of actual infinity, are a notable unpublished foundational stance on tame topology. Its kinship with mereotopology seems unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: Cor 1 opening: probably 'Idem pour figures F, G' rather than 'Il [?] pour figures'.
Cor 2: the image reads 'x ∥ F ⟺ x ≪̸ F' (crossed doubled '<', i.e. not ≪), consistent with 'x ∉ omb(F)', rather than 'x ≰ F'.
NB: 'les cadres auxquels j'ai songé pour [fins] pratiques' – likely 'fins pratiques'.
'(Axiomes de divisibilité)' is written underlined beneath 'les lieux (AtL 1,2,3)'; it may be singular, 'Axiome de divisibilité'.
AtL 1: in the image, 'Soit X ∈ M' is followed on a separate line by '∃ x ∈ L avec x ≪° X'.

Final paragraph roughly: 'Cet axiome d'apparence anodine implique pourtant (et signifie, en clair?) que les "espaces" ou "objets" ou "lieux" ... sont "infiniment divisibles" (et pas seulement qu'ils ne sont pas discrets) et à l'infini : c'est l'introduction de "l'infini actuel" tacite!' The last word looks like 'tacite' rather than 'donc'.
